classification.difficultyReason: Explain why percentages referring to different school populations cannot be added.

content.prompt: Explain why the following reasoning is incorrect. $20\%$ of the students going to one school have blond hair. $30\%$ of the students going to a nearby school have blond hair. Therefore, $20\%+30\%=50\%$ of the students in the two schools have blond hair.

answer.short: They are not percentages of the same whole.
answer.worked: The $20\%$ refers to students at the first school, while the $30\%$ refers to students at the nearby school. These are different wholes, so the percentages cannot be added to find the percentage for both schools combined.
